audioScript:
Woman: Who's that man? He's laughing a lot.
Boy: His name's Peter. He's always laughing.
Woman: That's nice.
Boy: Yes. He's very funny.

Woman: Who's the man with the black moustache?
Boy: That's Jim.
Woman: Look at all those cakes on his plate!
Boy: Yes. He's always hungry.

Woman: What's that woman doing?
Boy: I think she's making soup. She wants to put those vegetables in it. That's Daisy.
Woman: Is she good at cooking?
Boy: Yes, she is.

Boy: The woman with the curly grey hair's really nice.
Woman: Do you mean the one in the white sweater?
Boy: Yes.
Woman: What's her name?
Boy: It's Jane.

Boy: That person lives opposite us.
Woman: The woman who's carrying all the bowls?
Boy: Yes. She's putting the bowls on the table. She's called Sally.
Woman: Oh. How about going and talking to her?
Boy: Yes, let's do that now.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: Listen and write. There is one example.
audioScript:
Woman: Which sport do you like doing best at the sports centre?
Boy: I like swimming best.
Woman: Are you good at it?
Boy: I'm OK. I started swimming when I was five.
Woman: That's great.

Woman: Do you live near the sports centre?
Boy: Yes, in River Street.
Woman: Is that next to the river?
Boy: Yes, that's right. I often go for a walk there.

Woman: How do you come to the sports centre? By bike?
Boy: No. I come by bus. It's very quick.
Woman: Yes. And the bus is better when it's raining too.
Boy: Yes, it is.

Woman: When do you come to the sports centre?
Boy: I come after school.
Woman: Only after school?
Boy: Yes, that's right.

Woman: Do you sometimes buy things in the café?
Boy: I don't buy food. But I often buy some water when I'm thirsty.
Woman: Well, water's very good for you.
Boy: Yes.
Woman: So that's all. Thank you for answering my questions.
Boy: That's OK.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
Sally is telling her teacher, Mr Castle, about the people in her family and their jobs. What work do these people do?
Listen and write a letter in each box. There is one example.
audioScript:
Man: Does your mum work?
Girl: Yes, she does. She works at the new school.
Man: Oh? Is she a teacher there?
Girl: Well, she doesn't work in the classroom but she makes lunch for two hundred children every day because she's a cook there. She has to start at 7 o'clock every morning.
Man: Wow!

Girl: My grandpa lives in the city and he works, too.
Man: Does he? I didn't know that!
Girl: Yes, he can work because he isn't very old. I think he's fifty-five. He travels to lots of different places because he's a train driver. He thinks his work's brilliant!
Man: That's great!

Man: And I think your sister's too young to work.
Girl: She's only seventeen, but she does work. She's getting really famous now because she's often on TV.
Man: Wow! Is she a film star?
Girl: That's right, she is. I love watching her!
Man: Fantastic!

Man: What does your aunt do?
Girl: My aunt? Her name's Julia and she works at the hospital. She helps people who are ill.
Man: That's brilliant! Is she a doctor?
Girl: Yes. Everyone loves her because she's very good at her work!

Girl: My uncle works, too. But he doesn't work inside.
Man: Oh? Where does he work, then?
Girl: He works outside. And he loves singing when he's working. He's always doing that!
Man: What does he do?
Girl: He's got a huge farm and lots of animals to feed and look after. I love going there.
Man: That's nice!

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: Listen and tick (✓) the box. There is one example.

items.question: What job does Tom's sister have?
What did Alex do on holiday?
How did Jill help her mum and dad?
Which toy did Jack buy for his sister?

audioScript:
Man: Did you go to the movies yesterday, Anna?
Girl: I didn't want to see any of the films. I went shopping with my friends.
Man: Did you go to a café with them for lunch?
Girl: No. But we were very hungry when we got home and Mum made us some pasta.

Woman: Does your sister work for the hospital, Tom?
Boy: Yes, and my dad does too. He's a nurse there.
Woman: Is your sister a doctor?
Boy: No. She's a driver. She takes people to the hospital.

Woman: Did you go fishing with your dad on holiday, Alex?
Boy: No. That's boring. I had sailing lessons.
Woman: Did your brother do that too?
Boy: No. He played tennis every day.

Girl: We moved to a new house last week. It was a lot of work.
Man: Did you have to carry lots of boxes, Jill?
Girl: Dad did that. And Mum painted the kitchen. I washed all the cupboards.
Man: Good.

Man: What did you buy for your baby sister, Jack?
Boy: I saw a nice toy panda but she's got lots of animals.
Man: And she's too small for dolls.
Boy: Yes. So I got her this clown. When you pick it up, it laughs.

items.item: Longer scarf on the boy sitting down
Leaf that the girl is trying to catch
Ball that the boy is kicking

audioScript:
Girl: What shall I colour now?
Man: The teacher's drinking a cup of tea.
Girl: Shall I colour the cup that he's holding?
Man: Yes. Colour it orange, please.
Girl: OK. I'm doing that now.

Girl: The children who are sitting down are wearing scarves.
Man: Can you see the longer scarf?
Girl: Yes. Shall I colour it?
Man: OK. Colour it blue, please.
Girl: That's a nice colour.

Man: There aren't many leaves on the tree.
Girl: No. That girl is trying to catch one.
Man: Oh yes.
Girl: Shall I colour that leaf yellow?
Man: That's a good idea.

Man: Now I'd like you to write something.
Girl: OK then.
Man: Write the word STONE above the door of the small house.
Girl: That's easy! I can spell STONE!
Man: Brilliant!

Girl: That boy's playing with a ball.
Man: Yes. He's kicking it now.
Girl: What colour shall I do the ball?
Man: Colour it brown.
Girl: OK.
Man: Good. This picture looks better now.
